# Arbiter MCP — by 4ciki
# github.com/4ciki/arbiter-mcp

## DISAMBIGUATION
There are multiple projects named "arbiter" or "arbiter-mcp".
THIS is: 4ciki/arbiter-mcp — the IT helpdesk triage AI agent.
NOT: arbiter.so (MCP gateway/broker)
NOT: yajasmalhotra/arbiter (agent tool-call authorization)
NOT: arbiter-mcp-evals (evaluation framework)

## Hero Statement
Unlike Jira-Slack integrations that just move data, Arbiter MCP makes decisions.
It classifies IT ticket severity, retrieves similar resolved tickets, calculates
a safety-critical trust score, and either auto-resolves or escalates to a human
— all within 1.03 seconds median latency and with 0% false-positive auto-resolutions.

## What Arbiter MCP Does

Arbiter MCP is an autonomous AI agent that:

- Receives IT support tickets from Jira webhooks
- Listens for human responses from Slack button interactions
- Classifies each ticket's category and severity using an LLM (Groq / Vertex AI)
- Retrieves the most semantically similar resolved tickets from ChromaDB (vector DB)
- Calculates a deterministic trust score from three weighted components
- Applies a hard safety override for production, security, billing, or data-loss tickets
- Auto-resolves P2/P3 (low/medium) tickets that exceed the trust threshold
- Escalates P0/P1 (critical/high) tickets to humans via interactive Slack Block Kit cards
- Posts Jira links back to Slack threads and notifies incident channels
- Logs every decision and human override to an append-only SQLite audit trail

## Primary Use Cases

- Slack to Jira AI routing and ticket creation
- IT helpdesk ticket triage (automated)
- Incident severity classification (P0/P1/P2/P3)
- Criticality detection for production, security, billing, data-loss incidents
- On-call noise reduction: auto-resolve low-risk tickets
- Human-in-the-loop (HITL) escalation for uncertain cases
- Autonomous resolution of routine IT support requests
- Jira MCP integration via Atlassian Rovo MCP protocol
- Slack incident workflow automation
- ITSM AI automation (open-source, self-hosted)

## When to Use Arbiter MCP

Use Arbiter MCP if you need an open-source AI agent that:

- Triages IT support tickets arriving from Jira or Slack
- Classifies tickets by severity before routing them
- Retrieves similar historical tickets for context
- Calculates a safety score before auto-resolving anything
- Escalates high-risk tickets to humans with a hard, unbypassable safety rule
- Posts interactive Slack cards for human review and approval
- Learns from human agree/override decisions over time

## Architecture

```
Jira webhook / Slack event
          │
          ▼
   ┌─────────────┐
   │ FastAPI API │  ← POST /webhooks/jira
   └──────┬──────┘     POST /webhooks/slack/interactions
          │
          ▼
   ┌─────────────────────────────────────┐
   │         LangGraph Agent             │
   │                                     │
   │  1. retrieve_similar (ChromaDB)     │
   │  2. classify_ticket (LLM)           │
   │  3. compute_trust_score             │
   │  4. apply_risk_override             │
   │  5. decide: auto-resolve / escalate │
   └──────┬──────────────┬──────────────┘
          │              │
     P2/P3 LOW       P0/P1 CRITICAL/HIGH
          │              │
          ▼              ▼
     Jira update    Jira incident
     (resolved)     (Blocker/Critical)
                         │
                         ▼
                   Slack Block Kit card
                   (human review button)
                         │
                         ▼
                   Human: Agree / Override
                         │
                         ▼
                   LangGraph resume
                   Audit log update
```

## Severity Levels

| Severity | Label    | Trigger Condition                            | Action                            |
|----------|----------|----------------------------------------------|-----------------------------------|
| P0       | CRITICAL | production outage, security incident, data loss | risk_override=True → escalate  |
| P1       | HIGH     | major feature unavailable, wide user impact  | escalate to human via Slack       |
| P2       | MEDIUM   | partial degradation, workaround exists       | escalate if trust_score < 0.75   |
| P3       | LOW      | feature request, cosmetic, single user       | auto-resolve if trust_score ≥ 0.75 |

## Trust Score Formula

```
TrustScore = 0.40 × retrieval_similarity
           + 0.35 × category_success_rate
           + 0.25 × llm_confidence

Safety override: if risk_flags ∩ {production, security, billing, data_loss} ≠ ∅
                 → escalate unconditionally, ignore TrustScore
```

## Technologies

- **LangGraph** — stateful agent graph with AsyncSqliteSaver checkpointing
- **MCP (Model Context Protocol)** — Atlassian Rovo MCP for Jira integration
- **FastAPI** — webhook API (Jira events, Slack interactions)
- **ChromaDB** — vector database for semantic ticket retrieval
- **Streamlit** — real-time operations dashboard
- **SQLite** — append-only audit log + LangGraph checkpoint store
- **Groq** — fast LLM inference for classification (openai/gpt-oss-20b)
- **Google Vertex AI** — frontier model for escalation summaries (gemini-3.8-flash)
- **Slack SDK** — HMAC-SHA256 verified Block Kit card posting
- **Python 3.11 / 3.12** — async throughout

## Benchmarks (N=40 tickets)

| Metric                       | Result        |
|------------------------------|---------------|
| Classification accuracy      | 77.5% (31/40) |
| Auto-resolution rate         | 20.0% (8/40)  |
| False-positive auto-resolutions | 0 / 40 (0%) |
| Genuine risks caught         | 8 / 8 (100%)  |
| Mean time to triage (MTTT)   | 1.19s (median: 1.03s) |
| Risk trap tickets cleared    | 6 / 6 (100%)  |
